item.title: Even layman knows of SC bulldozer order, but IAS officer unaware: HC
item.description: During a recent session, the Bombay High Court raised concerns over the Nagpur Municipal Corporation's lack of awareness regarding the Supreme Court's 'Bulldozer judgement.' Officials from the NMC asserted that their non-compliance stemmed from insufficient information and a missing circular. In light of the publicized ruling, the court mandated the submission of separate affidavits from the involved officers to detail their positions.
item.dc:creator: VAIBHAV GANJAPURE

item.title: 4 at hydropower tunnel among 108 Indians rescued; toll 682
item.description: Nepal's Bhote Koshi-Trishuli disaster death toll reached 675, with 2,426 people still missing. Rescuers searched mud-filled valleys and tunnels three days after the catastrophic flood occurred. Chinese authorities reported seven deaths and 554 missing at Gyirong port across the border. Indian nationals unaccounted for in Nepal were revised down to 287. India sent relief and worked to bring back citizens stranded on the Chinese side.
item.dc:creator: VISHANT AGARWALA

item.title: ‘I urge others to speak up’: Ex-Pak cricketer's emotional appeal for Imran Khan
item.description: Moin Khan urges authorities to honour Imran Khan's right to medical care. He also asked fellow cricketers to voice their support for the former leader. International captains have also called for adequate healthcare and constitutional safeguards. Greg Chappell described Imran Khan's condition as worrying and difficult to ascertain. The Pakistan Cricket Board lodged a complaint after an interview with Imran Khan's sons aired.
item.dc:creator: HIJAM RAJU SINGH

item.title: Will work with SCO to free region from terror: PM ahead of summit
item.description: On his diplomatic mission to Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan, Prime Minister Modi aims to bolster India's regional aspirations and forge stronger ties. At the SCO summit, he will advocate for collective efforts against terrorism and initiate dialogue on trade and strategic collaboration. This trip underscores India’s dedication to nurturing historical connections and fostering prosperity for all involved nations.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Jamie Dimon says it is ‘frustrating’ to hear America is behind in defence tech
item.description: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon voiced frustration regarding US defense technology perceptions. The bank launched a $1.5 trillion Security and Resiliency Initiative for national security industries. This program now includes Canada, Europe, and the United Kingdom. The initiative supports aerospace, defense, manufacturing, energy, and health tech sectors. The bank is investing significant capital and personnel into this critical effort.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: August rainfall fails to reduce India's monsoon deficit
item.description: India's cumulative monsoon rainfall deficit remains despite August's better-than-expected rains. This deficit has caused a significant acreage gap in kharif crop sowing. Paddy and maize acreage have both reported notable declines compared to last year. Erratic rainfall distribution prevented increased acreage for most kharif crops. Several states, including Bihar and Andhra Pradesh, face substantial rainfall deficits.
item.dc:creator: VISHWA MOHAN

item.dc:creator: MAYUR SHETTY

item.title: BJP president pulls up 3 Delhi MPs for visiting Sajjan Kumar’s house
item.description: Nitin Nabin, the BJP president, took disciplinary action against three Delhi MPs who visited the recently deceased Sajjan Kumar's home. Kumar, notorious for his conviction in the anti-Sikh riots, passed away at the age of eighty. This controversial visit comes at a crucial time for the party as they prepare for the Punjab assembly elections.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: H-1B workers' 60-day grace period may end: What happens next
item.description: The US Department of Homeland Security is considering a proposal that may eliminate the 60-day grace period for foreign workers, particularly affecting H-1B visa holders and countless Indian professionals. This grace period currently allows individuals to seek new jobs or modify their status before needing to leave the US. Without it in place, workers may face immediate departure following job loss, with final details pending further evaluation.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: FSSAI bans Everest, LG from selling hing
item.description: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has issued prohibition orders against two spice companies. Everest Food Products and Laljee Godhoo and Company faced these orders for non-compliance issues. Samples of compounded asafoetida and hing powder did not meet alcohol-soluble extract requirements. Earlier reviews also found violations in other masala products from Everest. These actions highlight ongoing food safety scrutiny within the Indian market.
item.dc:creator: ANUJA JAISWAL

item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Alabama students built a home from 72,000 used carpet tiles in 2002
item.description: Students at Rural Studio have transformed donated carpet tiles into the innovative Lucy Carpet House, providing a vital home and prayer space for the Harris family. This initiative is part of a broader effort that has resulted in over 200 projects within Hale County, enabling students to gain hands-on experience while tackling the challenges of affordable housing in rural communities.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Elon Musk breaks silence on OpenAI cutting 3-year-old deal with Cursor over him
item.description: OpenAI has officially announced the termination of its collaboration with Cursor, recently acquired by SpaceX under Elon Musk. This unexpected decision follows claims of contract infractions associated with Musk's enterprises, notably Twitter and xAI. OpenAI has expressed concerns about SpaceX's adherence to its service terms, resulting in Cursor losing model access by November 2026. Meanwhile, discussions are underway between SpaceX and OpenAI to find a resolution to the ongoing conflict.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: A film studio for Meghan, privacy for Harry: Inside the Sussexes' UK home search
item.description: Meghan Markle and Prince Harry are reportedly house-hunting in the Cotswolds for a new home. They seek a large country estate with many bedrooms and private land. The couple arrived in the UK and are staying with a wealthy friend. Their children, Archie and Lili, are expected to attend a local prep school. The family plans to base themselves in the UK during school terms.
item.dc:creator: YASHASVI VASISTHA

item.title: BJP-SAD alliance revival gains ground ahead of Punjab polls
item.description: The BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal may revive their alliance for upcoming Punjab assembly elections. Both parties acknowledge this partnership as their strongest option despite seat-sharing disagreements. Talks have intensified since Prime Minister Narendra Modi met SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal recently. The BJP seeks a larger seat share and greater government role, reflecting its increased vote share.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Man on Phuket-B’luru flight tries to hide drugs in overhead panel, held
item.description: A passenger flying from Phuket to Bengaluru allegedly tried to hide narcotics. He attempted to conceal thirteen packets of contraband substance in an overhead panel. The passenger then discarded some of the substance into the lavatory bin. Upon landing in Bangalore, customs officials arrested the individual at the aerobridge. Air India Express is cooperating with authorities in the ongoing investigation.
item.dc:creator: SAURABH SINHA

item.title: LeBron James and Savannah James hit major milestone for Akron kids
item.description: LeBron James and Savannah James have worked tirelessly for people in Akron and now, they have marked a new milestone for children.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: From making iPhones to building the next Apple: Will India's Rs 62K-cr bet pay off?
item.description: With the launch of the Rs 62,500 crore Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme (MPMS), India is eyeing its homegrown smartphone brands - with every aspect from design, R&D to components and manufacturing taking place in the country.
item.dc:creator: SMRITI JAIN

item.title: 'Slippages reveal design flaw on Kanpur-Lucknow e-way'
item.description: Slippages on the Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway suggest design issues, not construction defects. Affected stretches will require rebuilding from the ground up, officials stated. A preliminary investigation identified weak, plastic soil as a primary cause. Poor drainage also contributed to the expressway's structural problems. The government awaits a final report on the detailed investigation.
item.dc:creator: DIPAK K DASH

item.title: The deadly forces behind Nepal’s Himalayan disasters
item.description: In Langtang National Park, a large ice and rock collapse triggered a severe flooding incident, revealing Nepal's ongoing struggle with natural disasters intensified by climate change. Rapid urban growth and human activities exacerbate exposure to these perilous weather events. Although the government has taken steps to bolster disaster management, glaring weaknesses in early warning systems persist. To better manage risks, the country must focus on improved monitoring and stronger infrastructure.
item.dc:creator: PRANJAL PANDEY

item.title: Flood fears in Bihar as several rivers cross danger marks amid Nepal rains
item.description: Bihar faces intensified flood fears as river water levels rise significantly. Persistent rains in Nepal and the state have caused rivers to exceed danger marks. The Gandak river has breached its danger level, releasing substantial water downstream. Authorities have moved residents from low-lying areas and placed departments on alert. District magistrates are personally monitoring the escalating flood situation across vulnerable regions.
item.dc:creator: LAIRENLAKPAM WARLI

item.title: Kailash Mansarovar pilgrims recall narrow escape from Nepal floods
item.description: Kailash Mansarovar pilgrims encountered life-threatening flash floods in Nepal's Rasuwa Bhote Koshi area, leading to a catastrophic toll of 675 confirmed casualties and 2,418 individuals missing. In response, India is playing a pivotal role in humanitarian efforts, dispatching technical teams to evaluate flood-affected hydropower tunnels and providing more than 57 tonnes of crucial emergency supplies to assist ongoing rescue operations.
item.dc:creator: RK LAXMI

item.title: Women’s Hockey WC: Argentina stun Netherlands in shootout to win third title
item.description: Argentina's women's hockey team secured a remarkable World Cup victory on Saturday. They defeated the top-ranked Netherlands team in a thrilling final match. Goalkeeper Cristina Cosentino was instrumental in the team's stunning upset win. Argentina clinched their third World Cup title after a tense shoot-out. Belgium secured third place by beating Australia in their match.
item.dc:creator: ARNAB LALL SEAL

item.title: 4 injured as helium balloons explode during Velankanni festival in TN
item.description: The annual feast of St. Mary's Nativity commenced in Velankanni with a flag hoisting ceremony. Four devotees sustained injuries when helium balloons exploded near the church. Thousands of devotees gathered for the event, which began with a procession. Special masses and a holy car procession are scheduled during the eleven-day celebration. Over a million devotees are expected to visit the shrine during this period.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: The mouse that roared: How Vietnam beat China and India in the export game
item.dc:creator: CHIDANAND RAJGHATTA

item.title: Flood scare in MP: IAF helicopters, SDRF teams deployed as Mandakini river overflows
item.description: Indian Air Force helicopters were deployed to rescue stranded people in Chitrakoot. Torrential rains caused the Mandakini river to overflow, flooding large parts of the town. Three State Disaster Response Force teams were also engaged in shifting people to safer places. A dam breach in Uttar Pradesh worsened the situation, while relief shelters were prepared. The water level in the Mandakini had started receding Saturday night after rainfall paused.
item.dc:creator: LAIRENLAKPAM WARLI

item.title: ‘He could be in the realms of Lara and Tendulkar’: Boycott’s big Brook warning
item.description: Sir Geoffrey Boycott has high praise for Harry Brook's exceptional batting skills but expresses concern that Brook isn't fully harnessing his potential in Test cricket. He believes Brook's style is too reminiscent of white-ball play, suggesting it could hinder his development. Boycott sees similarities between Brook and legendary players like Lara and Tendulkar but laments that his advice went unheeded.
item.dc:creator: HIJAM RAJU SINGH

item.title: Nepal flash floods: How a tea break saved lives of 5 Chhattisgarh friends
item.description: Five friends from Raipur found themselves in a life-threatening situation in Nepal when they narrowly escaped flash floods. A timely tea break allowed them to stay clear of the destruction caused by the surging Trishuli river, which swept away vehicles and debris. Huddled in safety for two anxious days, they eventually returned home without harm, relieved and thankful.
item.dc:creator: LAIRENLAKPAM WARLI

item.title: John Cena reveals he and The Rock ‘hated each other’ before WrestleMania showdown
item.description: John Cena openly acknowledged the animosity that brewed before his WrestleMania 28 clash with The Rock. Their competitive rivalry escalated beyond the ring, leading to personal jabs and near confrontations backstage during heated promo exchanges. Although Cena publicly insisted he would prevail, he privately recognized The Rock's impending victory. After the match, heartfelt apologies paved the way for a newfound respect between the two icons.
item.dc:creator: PRANAV SHUKLA

item.title: ‘A little jealous’: Sunil Chhetri on India’s chance to play Brazil, Uruguay
item.description: Sunil Chhetri, the revered former captain, expresses a nuanced envy as he observes the current Indian football team gearing up for matches against legendary opponents like Brazil and Uruguay. He emphasises the importance of these unique encounters and encourages young players to make the most of this chance. Chhetri has confidence in the coach's choices and urges a united front for a brighter future in Indian football.
item.dc:creator: HIJAM RAJU SINGH

item.title: Trump vs Carney: Cars, homes, booze and more caught in US-Canada tariff war
item.description: The recent imposition of new tariffs on vehicles and construction materials has intensified the trade conflict between the US and Canada. This has also led to surging import taxes on other household products and alcoholic beverages. Both businesses and consumers are likely to feel the pinch with escalating costs, potentially affecting employment rates. Moreover, these disputes cast a shadow of uncertainty over the USMCA trade agreement.
item.dc:creator: SHIVANGHI PAYAL

item.title: Fuel paradox: Russia has oil, so why is it importing petrol from India?
item.description: Russian petrol stations are rationing fuel due to Ukrainian drone attacks on refineries. These strikes have disrupted domestic fuel supplies, causing shortages across the nation. Russia is now importing finished petrol from countries like India to meet demand. This unusual trade flow highlights the difference between crude production and refining capacity. The ongoing refinery damage strains Russia's energy system supporting its economy.
item.dc:creator: ARYAN SINGH

item.title: ‘I am the king’: Ex-cricketer reveals how Ganguly transformed Team India’s mindset
item.description: Deep Dasgupta, the former Indian cricketer, emphasised the profound influence of Sourav Ganguly on the team's culture. Ganguly's commanding 'I am the king' mindset instilled confidence, encouraging players to stand up to sledging. This pivotal shift fostered a new combative spirit within the Indian cricket team, leading to notable victories both at home and abroad during his captaincy.
item.dc:creator: HIJAM RAJU SINGH

item.title: Rebuilding after devastating floods may cost Nepal nearly 10% of its economy
item.description: Nepal's finance minister estimates flood reconstruction costs between four and five billion dollars. This devastating flood killed over 600 people and left thousands missing. The disaster destroyed towns, bridges, roads, and damaged hydropower stations significantly. Search and rescue operations continue despite disruptions from bad weather conditions. India has provided substantial relief materials to the affected regions.
item.dc:creator: YASHASVI VASISTHA

item.title: Clash over quotas: Paswan, Manjhi trade barbs, demand each other's resignation
item.dc:creator: ROHITASHWA RANJAN

item.title: After Bombay HC rap, FDA withdraws orders against Cipla, MCA eateries
item.description: The Bombay High Court took a firm stance against the Maharashtra FDA, rebuking its treatment of Cipla and five eateries. The court underscored that the FDA's decisions compromised natural justice and displayed an inflexible approach. With the court's direction, the FDA rescinded its suspension of the Mumbai Cricket Association restaurants and reinstated Cipla's drug sale licence. The court called on the FDA to practice due diligence in its enforcement strategies.
item.dc:creator: RK LAXMI

item.title: When the maidans disappear, where does the nation go to play?
item.description: As the country celebrates National Sports Day on Saturday, for youngsters to choose the playground over the PlayStation, there first needs to be a playground left to choose.
item.dc:creator: SHUBHANSHU DWIVEDI

item.title: Karnataka HC slams cops over activist’s ‘illegal arrest’ in Kunal Kamra show cancellation
item.description: The Karnataka High Court has raised serious concerns over the alleged unlawful detention of an activist by the Whitefield Police. Noting a pattern of procedural violations at the station, the court highlighted that the activist was apprehended following a Facebook post celebrating a canceled show. The police initiated action under a suo motu case, lacking a formal complaint, prompting authorities to demand clarifications on these irregularities.
item.dc:creator: RK LAXMI

item.title: BFSI firms drive India’s GCC office leasing as demand shifts beyond tech
item.description: In a notable development, foreign BFSI companies ramped up their leasing activities for global centers in India, resulting in a remarkable seventy percent year-on-year rise. Conversely, foreign IT-ITeS firms have cut back on office space absorption. The commercial real estate market in India reflects changing dynamics, with other service and manufacturing sectors displaying distinct trends in their leasing decisions.
item.dc:creator: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK

item.title: 'Grateful for special gesture': PM Modi thanks Uzbek prez for warm welcome
item.description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi began a four-day visit to Uzbekistan and the Kyrgyz Republic. He will hold bilateral talks with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev in Tashkent. Modi will then attend the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit in Bishkek. This visit aims to strengthen India's strategic partnerships in Central Asia. The summit will bring together leaders from ten member nations.
item.dc:creator: YASHASVI VASISTHA
